sources.title: Gaussian boson sampling with 1,024 squeezed states in 8,176 modes
reconstructed_facts: The processor is identified as Jiuzhang 4.0.
The reported workload is Gaussian boson sampling.
The processor incorporates 1,024 squeezed states into an 8,176-mode circuit.
The paper reports detection events up to 3,050 photons.
The publication frames Gaussian boson sampling as a model for demonstrating quantum computational advantage and as relevant to bosonic error-correcting-code research toward fault tolerance.
non_inferences: This source does not by itself establish arbitrary-compute performance at the reported sampling advantage.
This source does not by itself establish execution of Shor's algorithm against RSA-2048 or ECC.
This source does not by itself establish operational decryption of captured Western communications.

sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.title: Post-Quantum Cryptography
reconstructed_facts: NIST finalized FIPS 203 (ML-KEM), FIPS 204 (ML-DSA), and FIPS 205 (SLH-DSA) in August 2024.
NIST states organizations should begin applying these standards now and begin migrating systems to quantum-resistant cryptography.
NIST identifies ML-KEM, ML-DSA, and SLH-DSA as standards ready for use now.
NIST transition planning targets deprecation and eventual removal of quantum-vulnerable algorithms from its standards by 2035, with higher-risk systems transitioning earlier.
sources.claim_effect: Contradicts any unqualified claim that deployable standardized quantum-resistant cryptography is unavailable.

sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.title: What Is Post-Quantum Cryptography?
reconstructed_facts: NIST states cryptographically relevant quantum computers do not exist yet.
NIST states timing estimates for a cryptographically relevant quantum computer vary widely.
NIST identifies harvest-now-decrypt-later as a present security reason to migrate before such a machine exists.
NIST states finalized post-quantum algorithms are ready for use and recommends transition begin immediately.
sources.claim_effect: Supports the risk of future quantum decryption and current HNDL exposure while not supporting a finding that RSA-2048 or ECC is presently operationally broken by a cryptographically relevant quantum computer.

sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.title: NIST IR 8547: Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards
reconstructed_facts: The transition document states that existing cryptographically relevant quantum computers do not currently threaten present security levels.
It emphasizes that cryptographic migrations can take more than a decade and therefore must begin before a CRQC exists.

sources.title: DeepSeek-V4 Preview: Entering the Era of Affordable Million-Token Context
reconstructed_facts: DeepSeek announced V4 Preview with a 1-million-token context length.
DeepSeek-V4-Pro is described as 1.6T total parameters with 49B active parameters.
DeepSeek-V4-Flash is described as 284B total parameters with 13B active parameters.
The release describes model capability, API availability, and open weights.
non_inferences: The DeepSeek release does not establish cryptographically relevant quantum-computing capability.
The DeepSeek release does not establish RSA/ECC decryption capability.
The existence of a strong AI model is not evidence that Jiuzhang's Gaussian-boson-sampling advantage transfers to cryptanalysis.
